keyVerseText: So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.
rootMeaning: The word πλήθω (plḗthō) is derived as a prolonged form of the primary Greek verb πλέω (pléō), which relates to the idea of filling or becoming full. This root sense conveys not merely a physical filling but also an imbibing or influencing, suggesting a comprehensive occupying or completion. Unlike the simple English gloss 'fill,' the root meaning encompasses both literal and figurative fullness, including the fulfillment of time or purpose, which enriches our understanding of its use in Scripture.
usageInScripture: Across its 24 occurrences, πλήθω is consistently translated with notions of being 'filled,' 'furnished,' or 'accomplished,' indicating both physical and metaphorical fullness. The top translations such as 'filled' (5 times), 'were accomplished' (4 times), and 'was filled' (3 times) reveal a broad semantic range that includes filling a space, fulfilling prophecy or time, and supplying or furnishing something. This diversity highlights the word's flexibility in describing both tangible and intangible forms of completion or abundance.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding πλήθω in its original sense deepens our grasp of God's providence and fulfillment of His promises. The verb's dual capacity to mean both literal filling and the fulfillment of time or prophecy underscores the sovereignty of God in orchestrating events to their divinely appointed completion. It reminds believers that God's work in the world is both abundant and purposeful, filling lives, hearts, and moments with His presence and plan. This fullness is not random but a deliberate accomplishment of His redemptive purposes through Christ, encouraging faith in God's perfect timing and provision.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 22:10 states, 'So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.' Here, πλήθω conveys the idea of the wedding being fully supplied or furnished with guests, emphasizing completeness and abundance. The word enriches this verse by highlighting not only the gathering but the satisfying fulfillment of the wedding feast, symbolizing the inclusive and ample provision of God's kingdom.
